newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Bank of Baroda listing halted in confusion.
newsitem.headline: India's Bank of Baroda listing halted in confusion.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) suspended trading in Bank of Baroda shares and cancelled early trades after a simultaneous listing on Friday of partly- and fully-paid shares confused investors, brokers said.
They said most investors were unsure which price quotes reflected the shares they held. Both partly- and fully-paid shares listed at around 35 rupees.
The BSE stopped trading in the state-run bank's shares as frantic traders tried to establish which shares they were dealing in.
The exchange later flashed an announcement on its online trading systems which said it had annnulled transactions in the shares.

The Bank of Baroda, among the country's five largest banks, issued 100 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 85 rupees a share in an initial public offer last December. The shares were listed on Friday.
Fully-paid shares jumped sharply to 82.25 rupees, after falling as low as 28 rupees in early trade.
For retail investors, employees and banks, the Bank of Baroda collected 25 rupees on application and 25 rupees on allotment. The balance will be collected later in the year.
Shares issued to non-resident Indians, overseas corporate bodies and foreign institutional investors were fully-paid shares at 85 rupees each.
